name: PricingCard
description: A pricing plan: name, price, what it includes and one call to action. A featured plan gets a brand border and a label such as "Most popular".
whenToUse: On a pricing page, one card per plan, side by side.
To compare plans where the price and included features matter most.

whenNotToUse.text: For a single upgrade offer inside a page.

anatomy.name: Features
anatomy.description: What is included, one per line.

anatomy.name: Action
anatomy.description: The call to action, usually a Button.

values.meaning: Highlighted with a brand border; use for one plan.

states.name: Featured
states.meaning: The highlighted plan with a brand border.

behavior.text: Keep the same feature order on every plan so the cards compare line by line.
Check marks and text align to the start in Arabic.

content: Name plans by who they are for: "Starter", "Pro", "Team".
Write features as short phrases, one per line.

guidelines.do: Feature one plan, the one most people should choose.
guidelines.why: A single highlight tells people which plan to start with.

guidelines.do: Keep feature lists in the same order across plans.
guidelines.dont: Reorder or rename features between plans.
guidelines.why: Matching rows let people compare the plans at a glance.

guidelines.do: Use one clear action per plan.
guidelines.dont: Put two primary buttons on one plan.
guidelines.why: Each plan should lead to one next step.

accessibility.role: article, named by the plan name.

aria.when: On the check marks, which are decorative.

accessibility.focus: The action button shows its own focus ring.

wcag.how: The plan name is a heading; features are a list.
The featured plan is also marked by its label, not only by its border.

notes: Price and period are read together so the amount is never separated from its billing period.

examples.title: Three plans
examples.description: A regular plan, a featured plan and an enterprise plan.
examples.code:
import { Button, PricingCard } from '@ds/react';

<PricingCard
  name="Pro"
  price="$29"
  period="per month"
  description="For growing teams."
  badge="Most popular"
  featured
  features={['Unlimited projects', 'Priority support']}
  action={<Button>Start free trial</Button>}
/>

examples.title: Free plan
examples.description: A regular plan with an outlined action.
examples.code:
import { Button, PricingCard } from '@ds/react';

<PricingCard name="Free" price="$0" features={['3 projects']} action={<Button variant="secondary" appearance="outline">Get started</Button>} />

examples.title: In a grid
examples.description: Plans side by side on a wide screen and stacked on a narrow one.

related.relation: For one upgrade offer inside a page.

components.name: PricingCard
components.description:
A pricing plan: name, price, what it includes and one call to action. Put the plan people are
most likely to choose in the featured position.

description.description: One or two lines on who the plan is for.

features.description: What is included, one item per line.

action.description: The call to action, usually a Button.

featured.description: Highlights the plan with a brand border.

--pricing-card-featured-border-color.description: Emphasized tone outline, e.g. a selected card.

--pricing-card-period-color.description: Supporting text on surfaces: descriptions, metadata, placeholders.

--pricing-card-description-color.description: Supporting text on surfaces: descriptions, metadata, placeholders.

--pricing-card-check-offset.description: Negative space (-4px) for deliberate overlap, e.g. stacked avatars.

--pricing-card-check-color.description: Main tone-colored text on light or tinted backgrounds: titles, active items.
